payload.textAr: The record decides what may be billed
payload.textEn: The record decides what may be billed

payload.mdAr:
A claim is a set of assertions about what happened. The record is the evidence for those assertions. When the two disagree, the record wins — not because it is more accurate, but because it is what a reviewer will read.

The working question is narrow and answerable: *for each line on this claim, is there something in the record that would satisfy someone who did not perform the service?* Not "did it probably happen", and not "is it usually done". Something written down.
payload.mdEn:
A claim is a set of assertions about what happened. The record is the evidence for those assertions. When the two disagree, the record wins — not because it is more accurate, but because it is what a reviewer will read.

The working question is narrow and answerable: *for each line on this claim, is there something in the record that would satisfy someone who did not perform the service?* Not "did it probably happen", and not "is it usually done". Something written down.

payload.defAr: A billed service is supported when the record independently shows it was performed and why. A note that describes an intention, an order, or a plan is not evidence that the service happened.
payload.defEn: A billed service is supported when the record independently shows it was performed and why. A note that describes an intention, an order, or a plan is not evidence that the service happened.

payload.defAr: Whether the service was appropriate for the documented condition. A service can be genuinely performed, correctly coded, and still unpayable because the record does not show why it was needed.
payload.defEn: Whether the service was appropriate for the documented condition. A service can be genuinely performed, correctly coded, and still unpayable because the record does not show why it was needed.
payload.exampleAr: Training example: imaging is documented as performed, but nothing in the record explains what question it was meant to answer.
payload.exampleEn: Training example: imaging is documented as performed, but nothing in the record explains what question it was meant to answer.

rows.textAr: Yes — the service and its performance are both stated.
rows.textEn: Yes — the service and its performance are both stated.

rows.textAr: No — an intention, not evidence that it happened.
rows.textEn: No — an intention, not evidence that it happened.

rows.textAr: "Two short follow-ups arranged over the next month."
rows.textEn: "Two short follow-ups arranged over the next month."

rows.textAr: Only once they occur; arranging is not delivering.
rows.textEn: Only once they occur; arranging is not delivering.

rows.textAr: No — the record does not support the level billed.
rows.textEn: No — the record does not support the level billed.

payload.mdAr: **Where this stops being a paperwork question.** Billing a level higher than the record supports is *upcoding*. Splitting one service into parts to be paid more is *unbundling*. Both can pass an automated edit, which is exactly why they are treated as integrity matters rather than errors — the system did not catch them, so a person is answerable for them. If a correction increases payment and the record did not change, stop and ask why.
payload.mdEn: **Where this stops being a paperwork question.** Billing a level higher than the record supports is *upcoding*. Splitting one service into parts to be paid more is *unbundling*. Both can pass an automated edit, which is exactly why they are treated as integrity matters rather than errors — the system did not catch them, so a person is answerable for them. If a correction increases payment and the record did not change, stop and ask why.

payload.mdAr: This pressure is usually not dramatic. It arrives as a suggestion that a code "probably" applies, or that a service is "always" done at this level. The defence is the same either way: point at the record. If the record does not say it, the claim should not either, and the person asking is better off knowing that before submission than after an audit.

itemsAr: For every line, ask whether the record would satisfy someone who did not perform the service.

A service can be real, correctly coded, and still unpayable if necessity is not documented.
Upcoding and unbundling often pass automated checks, which is why they are integrity matters rather than errors.

payload.textAr: Reading a record the way a reviewer does
payload.textEn: Reading a record the way a reviewer does

payload.promptAr: A claim bills an extended assessment and one follow-up visit. The record reads: "Extended assessment performed; findings recorded. Follow-up arranged for next month."
payload.promptEn: A claim bills an extended assessment and one follow-up visit. The record reads: "Extended assessment performed; findings recorded. Follow-up arranged for next month."

steps.showAr: Line 1: the record says the extended assessment was performed and the findings were recorded.
steps.showEn: Line 1: the record says the extended assessment was performed and the findings were recorded.
steps.whyAr: It states both the service and its performance, so it would satisfy someone who did not perform it.
steps.whyEn: It states both the service and its performance, so it would satisfy someone who did not perform it.

steps.showAr: Line 2: the record says the follow-up was arranged.
steps.showEn: Line 2: the record says the follow-up was arranged.
steps.whyAr: Arranging is an intention. It is not evidence that the visit happened.
steps.whyEn: Arranging is an intention. It is not evidence that the visit happened.

steps.showAr: Decide: bill line 1 now; line 2 waits until the follow-up occurs and is documented.
steps.showEn: Decide: bill line 1 now; line 2 waits until the follow-up occurs and is documented.
steps.whyAr: The claim has to say only what the record says. The record decides what may be billed.
steps.whyEn: The claim has to say only what the record says. The record decides what may be billed.

payload.answerAr: One line is supported and one is not yet. Billing the follow-up now would bill a plan.
payload.answerEn: One line is supported and one is not yet. Billing the follow-up now would bill a plan.

payload.situationAr: Reviewing a month of claims, you notice that one clinician's visits are billed at the highest assessment level far more often than colleagues' visits, and the notes behind them are brief and very similar to one another.
payload.situationEn: Reviewing a month of claims, you notice that one clinician's visits are billed at the highest assessment level far more often than colleagues' visits, and the notes behind them are brief and very similar to one another.

decisions.optionAr: Quietly downgrade those claims yourself before they go out.
decisions.optionEn: Quietly downgrade those claims yourself before they go out.
decisions.consequenceAr: You have changed claims without the record changing — the same move you noticed, in the other direction. The pattern itself is never examined, so it continues.
decisions.consequenceEn: You have changed claims without the record changing — the same move you noticed, in the other direction. The pattern itself is never examined, so it continues.

decisions.optionAr: Treat it as a pattern: raise it through the compliance route, citing the claims and what their records show.
decisions.optionEn: Treat it as a pattern: raise it through the compliance route, citing the claims and what their records show.
decisions.consequenceAr: A single mismatch is an error to correct; a repeated one is a pattern someone is answerable for. Pointing at the records keeps it about evidence rather than about the clinician.
decisions.consequenceEn: A single mismatch is an error to correct; a repeated one is a pattern someone is answerable for. Pointing at the records keeps it about evidence rather than about the clinician.

decisions.optionAr: Assume the clinician sees more complex patients and move on.
decisions.optionEn: Assume the clinician sees more complex patients and move on.
decisions.consequenceAr: Perhaps they do — but if the record does not show the complexity, the level is not supported. Assuming the best of a pattern is how upcoding persists.
decisions.consequenceEn: Perhaps they do — but if the record does not show the complexity, the level is not supported. Assuming the best of a pattern is how upcoding persists.
